les: Die gasse tussen plante en diere
kaps_punt: tydens fotosintese gebruik die plant koolstofdioksied uit die lug en gee suurstof aan die lug af; diere, insluitend mense, gebruik die suurstof uit die lug vir asemhaling en gee koolstofdioksied af wat deur plante vir fotosintese gebruik word

items.bewering: Asemhaling is om suurstof te gebruik om energie uit jou kos te kry. Daarby maak die lyf koolstofdioksied, wat die mens of dier dan afgee.
items.blok: Hoe mense en diere suurstof gebruik
items.bron: weet.co.za 'Asemhaling' (selrespirasie: oxygen used to burn carbohydrates and fats, releasing CO2); af.wikipedia 'Respirasie (fisiologie)' (sellulere respirasie). True as a description of aerobic cellular respiration; the word question is a separate item.

items.bewering: Mense en diere wat op land lewe, kry hulle suurstof uit die lug wat hulle inasem.
items.blok: Hoe mense en diere suurstof gebruik
items.bron: UPenn 'Diffusion: Allowing Earthworms to Breathe' and HowStuffWorks 'Earthworm Anatomy': earthworms have no lungs and take in oxygen by diffusion through moist skin; Ask A Biologist (ASU) 'How Do Insects Breathe?' and Wikipedia 'Respiratory system of insects': insects take air in through spiracles on the body sides, not through the mouth or nose
items.regstelling: The universal is false: every land animal is claimed to get its oxygen from air it breathes in, and an earthworm, which Grade 6 learners know well, takes oxygen through its damp skin and does not breathe in at all. Narrow the quantifier, not the subject: e.g. 'Mense en baie diere wat op land lewe, kry hulle suurstof uit die lug wat hulle inasem.' The oxygen still comes from the air, so the lesson's main point survives.

items.bewering: Die lug gaan deur jou neus of mond tot in jou longe. Wanneer jy uitasem, gaan die koolstofdioksied saam met die lug uit.
items.blok: Hoe mense en diere suurstof gebruik
items.bron: af.wikipedia 'Respirasie (fisiologie)': ventilasie is the in-and-out movement of air from the lungs; CO2 is removed through the respiratory system

items.bewering: Die meeste visse haal hulle suurstof met hulle kieue uit die water.
items.blok: Hoe mense en diere suurstof gebruik
items.bron: Britannica 'How Do Fish Breathe?'; Wikipedia 'Lungfish' (exceptions such as lungfish make 'die meeste' the correct quantifier)

items.bewering: Inasem en uitasem is dus nie self asemhaling nie. Dit is net hoe die gasse in en uit die lyf kom.
items.blok: Hoe mense en diere suurstof gebruik
items.bron: The science is right: breathing (ventilation) and cellular respiration are different processes. The claim, though, is about what the Afrikaans word means, and Afrikaans reference sources use 'asemhaling' for in-and-out breathing itself: af.wikipedia 'Respirasie (fisiologie)' says 'ventilasie (algemeen genoem asemhaling)', af.wikipedia 'Asemhaling' treats it as inaseming and uitaseming, and weet.co.za 'Asemhaling' uses the word for both. The lesson's own koolstofdioksied glossary entry uses 'asemhaal', the everyday breathing verb, for a process plants carry out too, although the lesson says plants 'asem nie in en uit nie'. A person must settle the terminology. Either keep 'asemhaling' for respiration only and remove 'asemhaal' from the glossary, or reword this sentence so it does not deny the everyday meaning.

items.bewering: Sit nou die twee kante saam ... 'n boom en 'n bok. Die boom gee tydens fotosintese suurstof aan die lug af. Die bok ... asem daardie lug in ... gebruik die suurstof vir asemhaling ... asem weer koolstofdioksied uit ... Die boom neem daardie koolstofdioksied deur sy blare in en gebruik dit vir fotosintese.
items.blok: Plante en diere hang aan mekaar
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Stoma'; Biology LibreTexts 16.2D; af.wikipedia 'Respirasie (fisiologie)'. Mapping checked: each gas goes in the right direction and there is no hint that plants breathe in or that animals make oxygen. The goat and tree are an illustration, not a closed two-organism cycle, and the block's own last sentence (other CO2 sources) prevents that reading.

items.bewering: suurstof: 'n Gas wat plante afgee wanneer hulle kos maak, en wat die meeste lewende dinge vir asemhaling gebruik.
items.blok: suurstof
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Anaerobic organism' and OpenStax Microbiology 9.2 'Oxygen Requirements for Microbial Growth': anaerobes are widespread among bacteria, archaea, protozoa and fungi, and no source found gives the proportion of all living things that use oxygen. Plants, animals and most fungi do use it. Naming the organisms makes the claim safe (e.g. 'wat mense, diere en plante vir asemhaling gebruik'). A person should decide, because this glossary entry may be a subject-wide wording.

items.bewering: koolstofdioksied: 'n Gas in die lug wat plante gebruik om kos te maak. Lewende dinge gee dit af wanneer hulle asemhaal.
items.blok: koolstofdioksied
items.bron: Biology LibreTexts 16.2D; KidsGardening (plants give off CO2 in respiration); Wikipedia 'Decomposer'. True if 'asemhaal' means respiration. Note: 'asemhaal' is ordinarily the breathing verb (af.wikipedia 'Asemhaling'), which clashes with the lesson saying a plant 'asem nie in en uit nie'. That is tied to the onseker item on the term.

items.bewering: asemhaling: Om suurstof te gebruik om energie uit jou kos te kry.
items.blok: asemhaling
items.bron: weet.co.za 'Asemhaling' (selrespirasie); af.wikipedia 'Respirasie (fisiologie)' (sellulere respirasie). This is accurate as a description of aerobic respiration. Whether the Afrikaans word may be given only this meaning is the onseker item.

opsomming: The photosynthesis and gas-exchange science is correct throughout. There is one error to fix: the lesson says every land animal gets oxygen from air it breathes in, and earthworms take it in through their skin. Two points need a person: the lesson says breathing in and out is 'nie self asemhaling nie', while Afrikaans sources use 'asemhaling' for breathing and the lesson's own glossary uses 'asemhaal'; and the glossary claim that 'die meeste lewende dinge' use oxygen cannot be verified once microbes are counted.
